question.prompt: The odd positive integers, \(1,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) \(7,\) \(\ldots,\) are arranged in five columns continuing with the pattern shown. Counting from the left, the column in which \(1985\) appears is the \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} &1&3&5&7\\ 15&13&11&9&\\ &17&19&21&23\\ 31&29&27&25&\\ &33&35&37&39\\ 47&45&43&41&\\ &49&51&53&55 \end{array} \]

solutions.explanation:
Following the odd numbers in increasing order, their column numbers repeat as
\[
2,3,4,5,4,3,2,1.
\]
One row moves right through columns \(2\) to \(5\), and the next moves left through columns \(4\) to \(1\). Thus each pair of rows gives one complete eight-entry cycle.

The \(n\)th odd positive integer is \(2n-1\), so \(1985\) is the
\[
\frac{1985+1}{2}=993\text{rd}
\]
odd positive integer. Since
\[
993=124\cdot8+1,
\]
\(124\) complete cycles account for the first \(992\) entries. Therefore \(1985\) is the first entry of the next cycle, which lies in the second column. The answer is choice B.
solutions.title: Locate the entry within a repeating block
